svg.title: Table layout check (dev, not a print component)
svg.desc: PROPOSED re-layout, not yet applied to the real board files. Constraint: Zone and Team are both true A4 landscape (297 x 210, no widening). Week is true A3 landscape (420 x 297, no extension). Reality is sized to fill whatever's left: 594 - 420 = 174 mm wide, matched to Week's 297mm height. The Event deck is explicitly excluded from the shared rectangle - it can sit anywhere on the table, no registration needed. This reverts THE TEAM's +36mm widen and THE PROJECT/SHIT HAPPENS's +35mm height extension from the previous check - see the follow-up note at the bottom for what that costs each real file. One example player board sits on each side. True 1:1 mm scale throughout. Not glued, not printed - open it in a browser. The placement-line layer prototypes the printed table-placement guide: only the seams that actually cross from one board to another are drawn (no outer-perimeter line) - each of the 5 board-to-board seams gets its own colour, drawn as a pair of 6mm-inset lines, one on each side of the seam. Correct assembly puts two same-coloured lines side by side; a board in the wrong slot, or rotated, shows up immediately as a colour that doesn't match its neighbour, or a line that doesn't line up with it - only one placement and orientation reads as correct.

PLAYER (N)
PLAYER (S)
WHAT THIS CHECKS

THE PROJECT, SHIT HAPPENS, THE TEAM and THE ZONE pack edge to edge into one 594 x 507 mm rectangle with zero gap - THE ZONE and THE TEAM both true A4 (297 x 210), THE PROJECT true A3 (420 x 297), SHIT HAPPENS resized to fill the rest (174 x 297). Follow-up needed on the real files: THE PROJECT loses its +35mm OVERTIME-slot extension, THE TEAM loses its +36mm widen (and STANDING's slot width needs re-checking), and SHIT HAPPENS shrinks on both dimensions - all three need their content re-fit before this is real, not just planned.
Per-player board - one of these per seat. Shown here for an example 4-player game, one per side; rotate to face however players actually sit.

Placement-line guide - 5 seams (4|3, 4|1, 3|1, 3|2, 1|2), each its own colour, a 6mm-inset line drawn by each of the two boards that share it. No outer-perimeter line: only crossings are marked. Matching colour + aligned lines confirms correct placement; either one being off exposes a wrong board, wrong slot, or wrong rotation.
The shared rectangle alone is 59.4 x 50.7 cm. With one player board on all four sides plus the event deck sitting outside it, the whole
layout needs about 90 x 80 cm - comfortably inside a standard dining table's width (~120 cm) and
close to its depth (most run 75-90 cm).
Re-open this file whenever a board's page size changes, or whenever seating/player count assumptions change.
